subject: Sierra.ai sierra-alpha latency variance / stability gate escalation
messages:
From: Ariel Summers <ops@sierra.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Sierra.ai Support <support@sierra.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Sep 2029 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Increased p95 and failed requests after sierra-alpha v2.1 rollout

Irene,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and a spike in 5xxs after your recent model rollout (sierra-alpha v2.1) that went live around 03:00 UTC this morning. Our front-end metrics show p95 jumping from ~210ms to ~780ms for inference calls to the endpoint that uses sierra-alpha. Error rate climbed to ~1.8% (was ~0.02%). Attaching sample graphs and a short CSV export.

Can you confirm if there was any change to routing, batching, or quantization profiles as part of the rollout? This is impacting live users — we may need a rollback if the root cause is model-side.

Att: sierra-prod-graphs-0904.png (PNG)

Thanks,
Ariel Summers
Ops Lead, Sierra.ai
ops@sierra.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Summers <ops@sierra.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Sep 2029 09:21:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p95 and failed requests after sierra-alpha v2.1 rollout

Thanks for the heads up, Ariel — we see the same signal in our telemetry.

Quick answers up-front: the rollout was a staged canary for sierra-alpha v2.1 (new attention kernels + different KV cache alignment) with a planned 10%->50% ramp. No changes to customer routing or throttle policy were made.

Marcus/Kim — I need a triage summary (p95 breakdown, affected regions/paths, release details) and a recommendation on rollback authorization. If rollback is the recommended remediation, we should also include an ask for a provisional SLA carveout (short window) so we can shift traffic and validate.

Ariel — we will loop you in within the hour with a remediation plan and ETA.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Ariel Summers <ops@sierra.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Sep 2029 10:05:12 -07:00
Subject: RE: Increased p95 and failed requests after sierra-alpha v2.1 rollout

I dug into the rollout logs and request traces. Summary:
- Correlation: 03:02 UTC rollout task triggered v2.1 on the primary pool for sierra-alpha.
- Metric impact: p95 increased from median 210ms to 820ms for requests routed to the updated pool; p50 unchanged.
- Error class: transient 504s and some kernel timeout retries observed on long sequence lengths (>1024 tokens).
- Regions: impact concentrated in us-west + us-east (matching customer traffic).

Preliminary hypothesis: the new attention kernel in v2.1 regresses for longer contexts — it increases per-token compute and causes KV cache pressure on current instance sizes. We also observed slightly different tensor layout that interacts poorly with our optimized cuBLAS path for that shape.

Recommendation: immediate rollback to sierra-alpha v2.0 in the affected pools, followed by a canary of v2.1 with a narrower seq-length distribution and increased request-level timeouts. Rollback plan attached (runbook-rollback-v2.0.md).

Operational asks for rollback:
- Authorization to execute rollback on the primary pools now (expected 7 minutes to route and validate).
- Provisional SLA carveout: 2 hours of leniency on p95 targets for this customer while we validate rollback and run a focused canary.

Irene/Kim — Marcus can run the rollback with my team if we have authorization.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Summers <ops@sierra.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Sep 2029 11:00:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p95 and failed requests after sierra-alpha v2.1 rollout

Ariel — thank you for the report and for attaching the graphs. We own the rollback decision here; our infra team recommends an immediate rollback to v2.0 for the primary pools to restore SLOs.

To be transparent on remediation and commercial impact: we are prepared to execute the rollback within 10 minutes of your go-ahead and will run a 20-minute validation canary before full traffic shift. If you prefer, we can also fail traffic to a secondary variant while we validate.

For cross-team coordination we are requesting:
- Customer authorization to proceed with rollback now.
- Agreement to a provisional SLA carveout for up to 2 hours (we will log precise window and provide post-mortem). During that window we may route small percentages through mitigation variants which could temporarily affect p95 visibility.
- Acceptance of a 10% bill credit for the affected hour as a gesture of goodwill if rollback is performed.

If you approve, we will:
1) Roll back v2.1 -> v2.0 on primary pool (Marcus)
2) Monitor p95 / error rate for 30 minutes
3) Share a post-action report and the runbook output

Please reply to this thread with AUTH or any other direction.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Account, Enterprise Sales
kimberly@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Ariel Summers <ops@sierra.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sierra.ai Support <support@sierra.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Sep 2029 11:22:49 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p95 and failed requests after sierra-alpha v2.1 rollout

AUTH. Please proceed with the rollback and keep us updated on ETA. We authorize the provisional 2-hour carveout for this event. Please confirm when the canary is green.

Thanks for the quick response.

Ariel Summers
Ops Lead, Sierra.ai
ops@sierra.ai
